newsitem.title: FINLAND: INTERVIEW - Helsinki telephone co plans listing.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Helsinki telephone co plans listing.

text.p: Helsinki telephone operator Helsingin Puhelin Yhdistys (HPY) is planning the first ever listing of a mutual telephone operator, said Jukka Ruuska, newly appointed corporate planning director.
HPY plans to offer shares in its operating arm Helsingin Puhelin Oy this autumn, and a listing is also on the agenda, Ruuska told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"The issue is planned for the autumn but there is no precise schedule," he said. A listing may be simultaneous with the issue or come later, he said.

Fifteen percent or some 5.9 million shares of a total 40 million would be on offer to domestic and international investors, and the company hopes for a market capitalisation of "closer to four billion markka than three billion," Ruuska said.
Four billion would be exactly the Helsinki Stock Exchange's average at end-December last year but just a fraction of telecommunications giant Nokia's 80 billion markka capitalisation.
The current owners of HPY -- about 420,000 subscribers with some 550,000 mutual shares -- would all have subscription rights but HPY aims for a clearly smaller amount of shareholders. @
The planned issue size would mean about 11 new shares per current mutual stake.
A market capitalisation of four billion would mean a share price of 100 markka while three billion would mean 75 markka.
"In initial plans, the value of the rights would be roughly a third of the market value of the stock available," he said.

Assessing Helsingin Puhelin's profit record is complicated by its mutual status -- much value-added has been returned to owners through pricing -- and by the fact that it has written off asset values over only 10 years, clearly faster than the industry standard depreciation, Ruuska said. @
"You can see up to twice that long depreciation plans (among other operators)," Ruuska said.
In 1995, Helsingin Puhelin group net sales were 1.96 billion markka, its gross margin was 522.2 million, the operating profit 72 million and the pretax profit 39 million markka.
In January-August 1996, net sales were 1.40 billion, the operating margin 342 million, the operating profit 55 million and the pretax profit 35 million markka.
Ruuska said the value of mutuality has been estimated to be some 300 million markka before tax. @
HPY and Helsingin Puhelin are currently seeking an adviser for the offering, and Ruuska said there has been a lot of interest. "We have plenty of friends," he said.
